tasks.title: Create Electron transparent overlay BrowserWindow
tasks.description: Implement src/main/avatar-window.ts and the initial src/main/main.ts skeleton. avatar-window.ts exports createAvatarWindow(bounds?) that creates a BrowserWindow with: frame:false, transparent:true, hasShadow:false, skipTaskbar:true, alwaysOnTop:true, focusable:false, thickFrame:false, roundedCorners:false, backgroundColor:'#00000000'. After creation call setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(true), setAlwaysOnTop(true,'floating'), and display with showInactive(). Implement setIgnoreMouseEvents(true,{forward:true}) by default; add an ipcMain.on('ptr-interactive-changed') handler that toggles it off/on. Add ipcMain.on handlers for 'drag-start', 'drag-move', 'drag-end' that use screen.getCursorScreenPoint() to reposition the window. main.ts calls app.whenReady(), creates the window with hardcoded default bounds (356x320), and loads the renderer index.html. State-store and sidecar integration are out of scope here (FEAT-07).
acceptance_criteria: npm run dev starts without errors and a transparent, frameless window appears on Windows
Window does not appear in the Windows taskbar
Window is always on top of other windows
Mouse clicks pass through the transparent background area (setIgnoreMouseEvents enabled by default)
Dragging the pet region (ipc: drag-start/drag-move/drag-end) moves the window via screen cursor position

tasks.title: Implement contextBridge preload API (petApi)
tasks.description: Implement src/preload/preload.ts to expose window.petApi via contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld. Define all IPC channel names as exported string constants at the top of the file (e.g. CH_STATE_SET, CH_STATE_CHANGE, CH_PTR_INTERACTIVE, CH_DRAG_START, CH_DRAG_MOVE, CH_DRAG_END). The petApi object must expose: setState(state:string) sends CH_STATE_SET to main via ipcRenderer.send; onStateChange(cb:(payload:{state:string})=>void) registers a once-per-message ipcRenderer.on listener for CH_STATE_CHANGE; setPointerInteractive(interactive:boolean) sends CH_PTR_INTERACTIVE; dragStart(offsetX:number,offsetY:number) sends CH_DRAG_START; dragMove() sends CH_DRAG_MOVE; dragEnd() sends CH_DRAG_END. Do not enable nodeIntegration. contextIsolation must be true (set in avatar-window.ts webPreferences).
acceptance_criteria: window.petApi is accessible in the Electron renderer DevTools console
All IPC channel name strings are defined as constants in one place in preload.ts
nodeIntegration is false in the BrowserWindow webPreferences
npm run lint passes with no TypeScript or ESLint errors

tasks.title: Implement state persistence module (state-store.ts)
tasks.description: Create src/main/state-store.ts. Define and export the AppState interface: { open: boolean, bounds: { x:number, y:number, width:number, height:number }, pet: { id:string, spritesheetPath:string, width:number, height:number, state:string }, byResolution: Record<string,{x:number,y:number,width:number,height:number}> }. Export loadState():AppState (reads %USERPROFILE%/.petdex-win/state.json with fs.readFileSync; returns defaults if missing or invalid), saveState(state:AppState):void, and saveBounds(bounds:Electron.Rectangle):void (updates bounds and byResolution keyed by '${width}x${height}'). Use os.homedir() to build the path. Create the .petdex-win directory with fs.mkdirSync({recursive:true}) if missing. All file I/O is synchronous. Default state: open:true, bounds:{x:1600,y:760,width:356,height:320}, pet:{id:'default',spritesheetPath:'',width:142,height:154,state:'idle'}.
acceptance_criteria: loadState() returns valid defaults when ~/.petdex-win/state.json does not exist
saveState() creates the ~/.petdex-win directory if it does not exist
A round-trip (saveState then loadState) preserves all fields without loss
saveBounds() updates byResolution keyed by the current screen resolution string
npm run lint passes

tasks.title: Build Svelte pet renderer with sprite animation state machine
tasks.description: Implement src/renderer/App.svelte and src/renderer/PetSprite.svelte. App.svelte mounts PetSprite and on mount calls window.petApi.onStateChange to receive state-change events from main, forwarding the new state into PetSprite via a Svelte reactive variable. PetSprite.svelte renders a <div data-avatar-mascot='true'> with inline CSS: background-image pointing to the spritesheet, background-size set to columns*100% by rows*100%, and background-position driven by the current frame. Load frame data from pets/default/pet.json (imported as a static JSON asset). The animation loop uses setInterval per-frame with the ms value from the frame entry; on state transitions, clear the previous interval. Implement once:true + fallback: after the last frame plays once, switch to the fallback state. Pointer handling: on pointermove, check event.target.closest('[data-avatar-mascot]') and call petApi.setPointerInteractive(bool). Drag: pointerdown calls petApi.dragStart(offsetX,offsetY), pointermove calls petApi.dragMove(), pointerup calls petApi.dragEnd(). Declare the petApi type on window in a src/renderer/env.d.ts file.
acceptance_criteria: Pet sprite renders on screen and plays the idle animation on startup
Calling petApi.setState('running') from DevTools switches to the running animation
A once:true state (jumping) automatically transitions to idle after one full loop
Hovering over the pet div calls setPointerInteractive(true); moving off calls setPointerInteractive(false)
Pointer-dragging the pet div triggers drag-start/drag-move/drag-end IPC events
npm run lint passes

tasks.title: Add system tray with Show/Hide/Quit
tasks.description: Create src/main/tray.ts. Export createTray(win:BrowserWindow):Tray and export a mutable isQuitting boolean flag. createTray creates a Tray using the icon at build/tray-icon.png (a 16x16 placeholder PNG — create a minimal 1x1 white PNG if no icon exists yet). Set a context menu with three items: 'Show Pet' calls win.showInactive(), 'Hide Pet' calls win.hide(), 'Quit' sets isQuitting=true and calls app.quit(). Also set the tray tooltip to 'buddy'. In main.ts, after creating the window, add a win.on('close') handler: if !isQuitting, call event.preventDefault() and win.hide(). This keeps the Electron process alive when the user closes the window. The tray icon must remain visible in the system tray while the app is running.
acceptance_criteria: A tray icon appears in the Windows system tray when the app runs
Clicking Hide Pet removes the window from view without quitting the process (tray icon remains)
Clicking Show Pet brings the window back using showInactive() without stealing focus
Clicking Quit fully terminates the Electron process
Closing the window with the system close button hides it rather than quitting
npm run lint passes

tasks.title: Implement local HTTP sidecar /state endpoint
tasks.description: Create src/main/sidecar.ts. Export startSidecar(win:BrowserWindow):http.Server and stopSidecar(server:http.Server):void. The server binds to 127.0.0.1 on BUDDY_PORT (process.env.BUDDY_PORT ?? 7777). On first run, generate a random 32-char hex token, write it to %USERPROFILE%/.petdex-win/runtime/update-token (create directories as needed), and read it back on subsequent runs. Handle POST /state: require Content-Type:application/json, parse body (max 4KB), validate X-Petdex-Update-Token header against the stored token, require a non-empty state string field, then call win.webContents.send('pet:state-change',{state}). Respond 200 {ok:true} on success. Handle GET /health: respond 200 {status:'ok'} with no token check. All other routes: 404. Wrong method on /state: 405. Bad payload: 400. Token mismatch: 401. All responses are JSON with Content-Type:application/json.
acceptance_criteria: GET /health returns {status:'ok'} with 200 without requiring a token
POST /state with correct token and {state:'running'} returns {ok:true} and triggers pet:state-change IPC
POST /state with missing or wrong token returns 401
POST /state with missing state field returns 400
Unknown routes return 404; wrong method on /state returns 405
The token file is created at ~/.petdex-win/runtime/update-token on first run
npm run lint passes

tasks.title: Wire main process — integrate modules, startup restore, bounds saving
tasks.description: Update src/main/main.ts to integrate all Phase 1 modules into a complete startup sequence. On app.whenReady(): (1) call loadState() to get persisted state; (2) create the overlay window via createAvatarWindow(state.bounds); (3) call createTray(win); (4) call startSidecar(win); (5) load the renderer (loadURL or loadFile for index.html); (6) wait for the renderer to signal ready via ipcMain.once('renderer-ready') before calling win.showInactive() if state.open is true. Wire bounds saving: on ipcMain.on('drag-end') call saveBounds(win.getBounds()); on screen.on('display-metrics-changed') call saveBounds(win.getBounds()); on win.on('close') (when isQuitting) call saveState({...loadState(), open:win.isVisible(), bounds:win.getBounds()}). On app.on('before-quit') set isQuitting=true, save final state, call stopSidecar. App.svelte must send 'renderer-ready' on mount so main knows the renderer is live before showing the window.
acceptance_criteria: App starts, renderer signals ready, window appears at the last saved position
Dragging the pet and restarting the app shows the pet at the dragged position
Changing display resolution saves the new bounds to state.json under byResolution
Quitting via tray persists the window open/closed state; restart respects it
npm run lint passes
npm run build completes without error (electron-forge packages the app as an npm-distributable binary)

tasks.title: Implement hooks install — Claude Code CLI and Codex CLI shell/config hooks
tasks.description:
Create src/main/hooks-install.ts. Export installHooks(options:{claudeCode?:boolean, codexCli?:boolean, shellRcPath?:string}):HookInstallResult where HookInstallResult is {installed:string[], skipped:string[], errors:string[]}. Both targets are CLI tools that can run in WSL or a Windows terminal. The hook event mapping is: UserPromptSubmit->jumping, PreToolUse->running, PostToolUse->idle, PermissionRequest->waiting, Stop->waving.

For Claude Code CLI: write hook entries to ~/.claude/settings.json (hooks section) and/or append shell rc lines to the target rc file (default: ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc based on SHELL env). Each hook entry calls petdex-bridge (or buddy state) with the appropriate state name and the sidecar update token. Check for existing entries before writing (idempotency).

For Codex CLI: append shell hook lines to the target rc file. If Codex CLI has a native hook config file, write entries there too using the same five event names (UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, Stop). Check for existing lines before appending (idempotency).

Export getHooksStatus(options:{claudeCode?:boolean, codexCli?:boolean, shellRcPath?:string}):Record<string,boolean> that checks which hooks are currently installed. This module must be callable from both the tray (add tray menu item Install Hooks that calls installHooks({claudeCode:true, codexCli:true}) and shows a dialog.showMessageBox result summary) and from the CLI layer (buddy hooks install subcommand, implemented in FEAT-09). Do not import Electron APIs at the module'''s top level — use dynamic requires so the module is importable from the CLI without loading Electron.
acceptance_criteria: installHooks({claudeCode:true, shellRcPath}) writes hook entries to ~/.claude/settings.json (hooks section) covering all five hook events (UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, Stop)
installHooks({codexCli:true, shellRcPath}) appends shell hook lines for Codex CLI to the specified rc file covering all five hook events
Re-running installHooks with either option is idempotent (no duplicate entries created in settings.json or rc files)
getHooksStatus() accurately reflects which Claude Code CLI and Codex CLI hooks are currently installed
The tray Install Hooks item calls installHooks({claudeCode:true, codexCli:true}) and shows a success/failure dialog
The module can be imported from the CLI (FEAT-09) without loading Electron (no top-level Electron import)
npm run lint passes

tasks.title: Implement buddy CLI entry point (start, stop, hooks install, state, doctor)
tasks.description: Create src/cli/index.ts as the npm bin entry point (registered as "buddy" in package.json bin field). Use commander or yargs for subcommand parsing. Implement five subcommands: (1) start — detect environment via /proc/version: on Windows spawn the Electron app process directly; in WSL invoke Windows-side buddy.exe via WSL interop (cmd.exe /c start buddy.exe); if interop is unavailable print a clear actionable error and exit non-zero. (2) stop — find and terminate the running Electron process by name. (3) hooks install — call installHooks() from hooks-install.ts with options derived from the current environment (codex:true on Windows, claudeCode:true in WSL writing to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc); print the HookInstallResult summary. (4) state <name> — read the update token from %USERPROFILE%/.petdex-win/runtime/update-token (Windows) or ~/.petdex-win/runtime/update-token (WSL), then POST {state:<name>} to http://127.0.0.1:${BUDDY_PORT}/state with X-Petdex-Update-Token header; print success or error. (5) doctor — check: Electron process is running, GET /health returns 200, update token file exists, hooks are installed (call getHooksStatus()); print a checklist with pass/fail for each item. Environment detection helper: export function isWSL():boolean that returns true when process.platform is linux and /proc/version contains Microsoft. All subcommands must work from both Windows (node.exe) and WSL (node). Do not import Electron directly in src/cli/ — it is not available in WSL.
acceptance_criteria: buddy start on Windows spawns the Electron process and the pet window appears
buddy start in WSL invokes buddy.exe via WSL interop and the pet window appears on the Windows desktop
buddy start in WSL without interop available prints a clear actionable error and exits non-zero
buddy hooks install on Windows writes Codex hook entries to %USERPROFILE%/.codex/hooks.json
buddy hooks install in WSL appends Claude Code shell hook lines to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc
buddy state running POSTs to the sidecar and the pet switches to the running animation
buddy doctor prints a pass/fail checklist covering process, sidecar, token, and hooks
isWSL() returns true in a WSL shell and false in a Windows cmd/PowerShell environment
src/cli/ imports no Electron modules (safe to run in WSL node)
npm run lint passes
